messages:
Alice Chen: Kicking off progressive rollout for release v2.3.1 in tonight's change window (22:00-02:00 UTC). Plan: US -> EU -> APAC, canary 2% then 25% then full. Release notes: https://redwood.example/releases/v2.3.1 :rocket:

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by Alice Chen for region=us-west, version=v2.3.1, strategy=canary(2%)

Bob Nguyen: Infra: US capacity looks good — GPU pools at ~70% free, expected headroom for canary. EU has scheduled DB maintenance at 23:30 UTC; suggest gating EU until maintenance completes.

Carol Martinez: Noted. I'll postpone EU until maintenance finishes +15m. APAC capacity is tight — only 1 spare node in apac-east, recommend very small canary (0.5%) and watch token-level latency.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment completed in US (region=us-west), healthchecks=PASS, avg latency +4ms, error_rate 0.1% :white_check_mark:

Dave Rao: Rollout decision: proceed to US ramp to 25% while we hold EU. Pinning to v2.3.1 (do not auto-rollout v2.3.2) — config set: pinned_version=v2.3.1

SRE-Sarah: Adding SLO alert thresholds: latency >200ms or error_rate>1% triggers immediate rollback. Oncall: @ops-oncall

ops-oncall: Copy. Rollback runbook at https://redwood.example/runbooks/rollback. If needed run:
```
redwoodctl rollback --region us-west --to-version v2.3.0 --force
```
I'll be monitoring.

deploy-bot: US ramp to 25% complete. CPU/GPU utilization within expected bounds. Token throughput steady.

Carol Martinez: Observability note — enabling extra traces for the user-facing route /api/generate for next 30m.

Bob Nguyen: EU gate remains closed until maintenance clear. I'll notify when DB migrations done.

deploy-bot: Attempting APAC canary (apac-east) with very small footprint: instance_type=g4-small, canary=0.5% — queued due to capacity.

Carol Martinez: APAC queued due to node shortage. Options: a) borrow burst capacity from Dedicated (slower) or b) wait 45m for nightly batch jobs to finish. My vote: wait 45m.

Alice Chen: OK we wait on APAC. Proceeding with US ramp to 60% over next 30m. Keep EU blocked. If any SRE alerts, abort and rollback to v2.3.0.

deploy-bot: US ramp to 60% in progress — ETA 28m.

Dave Rao: Leaving note: release notes updated with known issues (minor truncation bug) — acceptance criteria: monitor sample prompts for truncation. Link: https://redwood.example/releases/v2.3.1#known-issues

SRE-Sarah: Observability shows a 10% increase in tail latency for long requests (>5k tokens). Watching. If tail >25% then rollback.

ops-oncall: No action yet, watching logs and traces. Will call for rollback if thresholds hit.

deploy-bot: US ramp complete to 60%. Monitoring for 15m baseline.

Alice Chen: Thanks everyone. New plan: if US stable at 60% for 15m, we schedule EU ramp immediately after the DB maintenance window ends (23:45 UTC). APAC remains pending.

Bob Nguyen: DB maintenance done at 23:32 UTC. EU gate cleared. I'll do a quick smoke at 23:40 and then deploy-bot can start EU canary at 23:45.

deploy-bot: EU canary started (region=eu-central), canary=2%.

Carol Martinez: EU canary healthchecks PASS. Latency looks OK. Proceeding to ramp to 25%.

deploy-bot: EU ramp to 25% complete. All good.

Alice Chen: Final check before APAC: Carol, can you re-run capacity check in 20m and confirm we can do 1% canary without borrowing capacity?

Carol Martinez: Will do. If still tight, we'll coordinate a short burst from Dedicated and revert if cost spikes.

Bob Nguyen: FYI I've left a note to finance about possible burst billing for APAC if we borrow capacity.

deploy-bot: Thread marked for monitoring by Alice Chen — ongoing. Ping if thresholds cross.

Alice Chen: Closing — posting deployment summary in #releases later today. :tada:
